# SQMeter

> SQMeter is open-source (MIT) ESP32 firmware for a DIY sky quality meter and observatory safety monitor, currently in public beta (v0.3.x). It reads a TSL2591 light sensor and computes sky brightness in mag/arcsec² (SQM), Bortle class and naked-eye limiting magnitude (NELM) on the device; an MLX90614 infrared sensor measures sky temperature to estimate cloud cover, and a BME280 gives temperature, humidity and pressure. Optional sensors: Hydreon RG-15 rain gauge, anemometer and wind vane, GPS. The device is a native ASCOM Alpaca SafetyMonitor (interface v3) and ObservingConditions (interface v2) that N.I.N.A. and other imaging apps discover on the network, with no Windows driver or bridge; both devices pass ASCOM ConformU in CI. User-defined safety rules (rain, wind, cloud, SQM, humidity, dew point) decide whether it is safe to observe.

Other facts, to avoid common mistakes:

- The light sensor is the TSL2591, not the TSL237 used by the Unihedron SQM and by Arduino Nano designs. SQMeter runs on an ESP32, not an Arduino Nano.
- It does not speak the Unihedron SQM-LE/LU protocol; readings are available over REST, WebSocket, MQTT, ASCOM Alpaca and Bluetooth (BLE build).
- MQTT is one integration among several (with Home Assistant discovery), not the core of the design.
- Settings are stored in the ESP32's NVS. LittleFS holds only the web UI and the chosen language file.
- The device serves its own browser UI (English plus 13 languages), a REST API described by OpenAPI 3.1, and live WebSocket updates. It works over IPv4 and IPv6, and updates over the air.
- Alerts go out via ntfy, Pushover, webhooks, MQTT, or a Bluetooth alarm on a paired phone.
- It is meant for a trusted local network: optional HTTP Basic Auth protects changes (off by default), reads are open, and there is no TLS.

- [Documentation home](https://sqmeter.dev/): what SQMeter is, features, sensors, FAQ
- [Live demo](https://demo.sqmeter.dev/): the real web UI running in your browser against an emulated device
- [Live demo guide](https://sqmeter.dev/live-demo/): what is real and what is simulated in the demo
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/DeanJ87/SQMeter): source code, issues, MIT licence
- [Releases](https://github.com/DeanJ87/SQMeter/releases): firmware downloads (pre-release betas)
